Broken Promises: Eastern Cape

By: Sipha Kema | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A Trail of Broken Promises and Squandered Funds in the Eastern Cape...

Unique Selling Point:
Uncovering the hidden realities behind the facade of development in the Eastern Cape and exposing the cost of incomplete projects and hold accountable those responsible for the mismanagement of public funds. The pursuit of accountability for years-old projects that have been abandoned, showcasing the ongoing lack of oversight and transparency in local government spending.

Summary:
Amidst the buzz of provincial elections, Carte Blanche sets out to uncover a shadowy reality lurking beneath the surface of the Eastern Cape's development landscape. While the spotlight often shines on big-ticket projects and political promises, our investigation aims to shed light on the trail of incomplete projects left in the wake of mismanagement and controversy. This will be a news report.
At the heart of our story are the communities of the Eastern Cape, whose hopes for improved infrastructure and amenities have been dashed by a series of failed projects. From the bustling streets of Centane to the tranquil fields of eNgcobo, we will journey through the province to witness firsthand the remnants of projects that never reached fruition.


Further information:
Our investigation will start In Centane, our cameras will capture the surreal sight of a taxi rank that swallowed a whopping 6.4 million rand in public funds, yet fails to serve its intended purpose. Through investigative documents and interviews with stakeholders and officials, we will unravel the tangled web of bureaucracy and mismanagement that allowed such a debacle to occur.
We will turn our attention to the eNgcobo sports field, where 10 million rand vanished into thin air, leaving behind nothing but a desolate landscape and the echoes of broken promises. With drone footage and eyewitness accounts, we will paint a vivid picture of the human cost of unfinished projects and the toll they take on communities striving for progress.

Moving eastward, we will delve into the case of Sakhisizwe Local Municipality, where 23 million rand was poured into a sports facility that stands as a stark reminder of wasted resources and broken promises. With photographic evidence in hand, we will reveal the stark juxtaposition between the grand visions of the project and its current state of disrepair.


Emalahleni Local Municipality, where a staggering 11 million rand was allocated to an incomplete project now reduced to nothing more than overgrown grass. Through on-the-ground interviews and expert analysis, we will uncover the reasons behind the project's abandonment and examine the repercussions for local residents left in its wake.

Expose the truth behind the facade of development in the Eastern Cape, holding accountable those responsible for the squandering of public funds and the betrayal of public trust. In a province rife with political maneuvering and electoral fervor, our story will serve as a sobering reminder of the real-world consequences of incomplete projects and the urgent need for transparency and accountability in governance.

Press Release:


Broken Promises | Eastern Cape  

In the Eastern Cape, thousands of young, talented athletes with the potential to be tomorrow’s sports heroes, don’t have access to proper facilities. In villages across the province, netball courts, rugby fields and athletics tracks, are a rare sight, so when the provincial government promised the rural community of Sakhisizwe, that it would build a new multi-million-rand stadium, it was a welcomed development. Fast forward several years, and the much-anticipated high-performance centre, has become little more than an abandoned and unkept field. But it’s not the only community that’s been promised new or refurbished facilities costing millions, only for developers to pocket the money and fail to deliver. In this election campaign, Carte Blanche criss-crossed the province tracking several costly infrastructure projects in one of the poorest parts of the country, and what we find, is an expensive trail of broken promises.  

Producer: Sipha Kema | Presenter: Claire Mawisa  



Script:


BROKEN PROMISES EC – Script
Producer: Sipha Kema
Presenter: Claire Mawisa
Camera: Anton Scholtz
Editor: Stenette
DELIVERY 5 MAY 2024 ⦿
VO
The Eastern Cape, a province of diverse landscapes, and a rich history and culture…


You’d think it deserves significant investment… and yes, big money has been spent…



VO
Mdantsane has a public swimming pool with a R30 million price tag. The one in Butterworth is slightly more modest …

Not-so-state-of-the-art sports facilities…


Claire UPS
This is R23 million
VO
Then, there’s this transport hub that services 100’s of commuters each day…
Claire UPS
This is 6.8 million rand


[Fade to black]
LINK
In the heart of the Eastern Cape lies a tale of shattered dreams and broken promises. We’ve been told about development projects that haven’t lived up to what was promised by municipalities. We’re here to see for ourselves, were these communities short-changed?
VO
We’re focussing on smaller, often forgotten areas, starting in Centane. A small rural town surrounded by a cluster of over 20 villages, it’s the central transport node.

(Three beats…)

Like the rest of the country, taxis are vital to keeping the economy moving, and related infrastructure should be a government priority.




Amid much fanfare seven years ago, the local municipality prepared to hand over what it called a transport hub, which had cost R6.8 million.

Xolani Somana is the local chairman of the Border Taxi Association.

(two beats)

He tells me – his and another association called Ncedo and Border – initially refused to use the rank. Looking around, it’s not hard to see why.


UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA; CENTANE BORDER ASSOCIATION CHAIR
TIMECODES: 01:34 - 01:51


First of all they made it small, that is the first
thing, it does not fit the cars that are available in Centane
CLAIRE: So they don’t fit?
X: XOLANI: They don’t fit there and there’s water leaking everywhere.
VO
Yes, close to 7 million Rand later, a lack of drainage and the way the rank’s positioned sees passengers trudging through a deluge.
UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA; CENTANE BORDER ASSOCIATION CHAIR
SUBTITLES
02:06 - 02:13
When it rains people’s belongings get wet. It floods.
CLAIRE: (Claire’s reaction)
XOLANI: Yes, because we load passengers outside not underneath the shelter.
VO
Oddly, this site could have accommodated a much bigger structure.


UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA; CENTANE BORDER ASSOCIATION CHAIR
SUBTITLES
02:37 - 02:41
Do you have working toilets?

The toilets do not work. They worked for a short while then water starting leaking everywhere.
VO
When sewage overran the rank, the associations closed off the water supply.


UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA; CENTANE BORDER ASSOCIATION CHAIR
SUBTITLES
04:10 - 04:23


People have no place to relieve themselves when they need the loo, they have to use the bush. It’s a problem.
CLAIRE: CLAIRE’S REACTION - And you work long hours…
Xolani (04:19): We, the people who work here, also suffer because we live in the villages.
Once you get here and need the loo it becomes difficult.
VO
It’s impossible to see what 6.8 million has been spent on.


UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA; CENTANE BORDER ASSOCIATION CHAIR
04:42 - 05:01
It could never be that amount. Even if they say I don’t know about such things. It could never
be that amount. With this rank that I see before me, it was built with lesser money because we’ve build our own houses that are much bigger than these offices so we know about the costing.


VO
Leaving behind Centane’s pricey, flood-friendly taxi rank, we venture into the Province’s foothills.
LINK
So, I’m on my way to Sakhisizwe to meet a very active community member uBhuti Lungisile and he is going to tell me about a sports facility that has been built in his community, that’s apparently worth…R23 million rand



UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER
SUBTITLES
00:30


Lungisile we are here at your R23 million stadium, but I don't see the R23 million… Do you see it?

Early in 2017
00:39
We were very excited as a community when we were told that there will be a new stadium, we say it is a stadium because they told us they would be opening a stadium worth that amount that was mentioned but we are struggling to see the value now…


VO
Sakhisizwe, a township in Khowa, formerly Elliot, offers few opportunities. Sport is one of the few distractions for a troubled community.
UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER
SUBTITLES
01:15 - 01:32


Look at this athletic track, it should be made out of rubber so the children can have a sturdy and soft track. They run barefoot they get cut under their feet leaving them with sores because this cement has open cracks and crumbling.
VO
But hey, at least they got the promised netball court and athletics track….. The gym, tennis courts, and usable rugby and soccer fields were conspicuous by their absence?
UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER
SUBTITLES
01:47- 01:49


As the community we wanted to encourage some of the largely unavailable sports like power lifting, boxing, tennis, we have people who can train the youth for netball.
07:39 - 07:44
Rugby, it doesn’t exist, as you see the rugby poles…


UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER


This is the soil, as you can see from the small rocks, it’s concrete, they just added a topping, you see that layer?
Claire: This layer is so thin, look…
Lungisile: I’m sure they were replacing the track rubber…
Claire: This is not serious…
Lungisile 02:30 - 02:42: It’s thin, thin, thin and it will peel off very quickly, all this part they had started will
disappear, it will all finish.


VO
At this landmark project, the toilets don’t work and the electricity and plumbing have never been connected.


UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER


7:12Lungisile:
Look, there's no door.
Claire: Gone
07:14 Lungisile:
The smell, you can tell there's a problem.

07:20: And I don't know why they don't close this place…
07:22: They must close it because people are going to use it…
VO
This is what R23 million has built: a facility so unique it took three different contractors to NOT finish it.


VO
In the 2017/2018 financial year, the municipality set aside R12.5 million for its construction…
by 2020 the budget had doubled.
UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER
SUBTITLES
03:48 - 03:50
Sir, this stadium is a disappointment though, if we are being honest.

Yes, if we are being honest.


VO
But, 50 km away, in eNgcobo, things were about to get worse:

Here, allleged corruption and incompetence had seen yet another promise broken.


VO
I’m met by community activist, Tando Tunce.
UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE; SANCO SECRETARY
01:28 - 01:39


So, Tando, maybe you can tell us, where are we, what is this place and what is
it supposed to be?

This place is supposed to be a stadium, but when you look at it, it’s a bush that has things that show that there is somewhat of a stadium.
VO
This stadium was once at the heart of the district.
UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE; SANCO SECRETARY
02:28 - 02:35


It was a beautiful place that encouraged us and all the young people from the villages had a dream that one day they would come play sports here.
VO
In 2015 the sportsground was approved for an upgrade…

..with stands and a proper athletics rubber track already in place… it only needed a little facelift…
UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE; SANCO SECRETARY
03:25 - 03:37


This stadium was set to be built for R13,7 million but when it was built they topped up by an amount of R10 million to try ensure that the stadium is completed.
03:47 - 03:54
it was found that there was corruption happening in this stadium which led to halting the building process.
VO
Turns out, much like Centane and Sakhisizwe, it boasts features like toilets without plumbing or electricity… with predictable results.
UPS CLAIRE
I know as a CB presenter I’m supposed to go anywhere, but I think I’m going to stay outside for this one….
VO
But 23.7 million did buy some stands and a netball court.
UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE; SANCO SECRETARY
02:54 - 03:10


We feel extremely hurt as the people from eNgcobo from the players and organizers of soccer functions to the people at large because soccer and other sports help remove the youth from drugs.


V/O
In a statement - Dr AB Xuma Local Municipality confirmed that the project is still suspended due to substandard work and administration by the appointed contractor.
VO
We sought answers from the Eastern Cape Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs.


VO
After days of negotiation, the MEC agreed to an interview…


VO
But, after waiting for more than an hour, the MEC’s spokesperson and Chief of Staff appeared. Our cameras were rolling.
UPS
The interview is canceled for today
VO
But, not even the online interview materialised.
LINK
I have been stood up for the second time by COGTA MEC, Mr Zolile Williams.He had agreed to do a virtual interview with us to discuss these unfinished projects, but right now, not even his office is answering our calls.


V/O
The MEC later expressed disappointment with the state of the abandoned stadiums as these were meant to benefit local communities.

But he says 60% of all sports facilities and stadiums built in the past seven-and-a-half years are in good condition, adding that some are state of the art facilities in rural towns like Cofimvaba and Ntabankulu.

The MEC confirmed that investigations are underway in respect of the abandoned stadiums and that those responsible will be held accountable.




LINK
It's frustrating when money is allocated to build a facility and instead of just doing what you were meant to do with the money, there is nothing to show for it. And who suffers most? Children. Young people in the community, those with talent but have no opportunity to develop that talent.
VO
We leave amid Promises broken and unanswered questions.




PROMO 1 21”
Big money wasted and communities left with broken promises..

UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE
It was a beautiful place that encouraged us and all the young people from the villages had a dream that one day they would come play sports here.

The Eastern Cape is scattered with substandard, incomplete projects intended to improve the lives of the residents…
PROMO 2 21”
So-called State-of-the-art facilities built for the people of the Eastern Cape…

UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA They run barefoot, they get cut under their feet leaving them with sores because this cement has open cracks and crumbling.

Are communities benefiting from the millions being spent?
PROMO 3 21”
Incomplete, defunct sports stadiums and a taxi rank without working toilets…

UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA
People have no place to relieve themselves when they need the loo, they have to use the bush.

LINK this is R6.8 million rand!

The EC, a province of broken promises…

UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA; CENTANE BORDER ASSOCIATION CHAIR SUBTITLES 02:37 - 02:41 Do you have working toilets? The toilets do not work. They worked for a short while then water starting leaking everywhere. VO When sewage overran the rank, the associations closed off the water supply. UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA; CENTANE BORDER ASSOCIATION CHAIR SUBTITLES 04:10 - 04:23 People have no place to relieve themselves when they need the loo, they have to use the bush. It’s a problem. CLAIRE: CLAIRE’S REACTION - And you work long hours… Xolani (04:19): We, the people who work here, also suffer because we live in the villages. Once you get here and need the loo it becomes difficult. VO It’s impossible to see what 6.8 million has been spent on. UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA; CENTANE BORDER ASSOCIATION CHAIR 04:42 - 05:01 It could never be that amount. Even if they say I don’t know about such things. It could never be that amount. With this rank that I see before me, it was built with lesser money because we’ve build our own houses that are much bigger than these offices so we know about the costing. VO Leaving behind Centane’s pricey, flood-friendly taxi rank, we venture into the Province’s foothills. LINK So, I’m on my way to Sakhisizwe to meet a very active community member uBhuti Lungisile and he is going to tell me about a sports facility that has been built in his community, that’s apparently worth…R23 million rand UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER SUBTITLES 00:30 Lungisile we are here at your R23 million stadium, but I don't see the R23 million… Do you see it? Early in 2017 00:39 We were very excited as a community when we were told that there will be a new stadium, we say it is a stadium because they told us they would be opening a stadium worth that amount that was mentioned but we are struggling to see the value now… VO Sakhisizwe, a township in Khowa, formerly Elliot, offers few opportunities. Sport is one of the few distractions for a troubled community. UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER SUBTITLES 01:15 - 01:32 Look at this athletic track, it should be made out of rubber so the children can have a sturdy and soft track. They run barefoot they get cut under their feet leaving them with sores because this cement has open cracks and crumbling. VO But hey, at least they got the promised netball court and athletics track….. The gym, tennis courts, and usable rugby and soccer fields were conspicuous by their absence? UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER SUBTITLES 01:47- 01:49 As the community we wanted to encourage some of the largely unavailable sports like power lifting, boxing, tennis, we have people who can train the youth for netball. 07:39 - 07:44 Rugby, it doesn’t exist, as you see the rugby poles… UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER This is the soil, as you can see from the small rocks, it’s concrete, they just added a topping, you see that layer? Claire: This layer is so thin, look… Lungisile: I’m sure they were replacing the track rubber… Claire: This is not serious… Lungisile 02:30 - 02:42: It’s thin, thin, thin and it will peel off very quickly, all this part they had started will disappear, it will all finish. VO At this landmark project, the toilets don’t work and the electricity and plumbing have never been connected. UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER 7:12Lungisile: Look, there's no door. Claire: Gone 07:14 Lungisile: The smell, you can tell there's a problem. 07:20: And I don't know why they don't close this place… 07:22: They must close it because people are going to use it… VO This is what R23 million has built: a facility so unique it took three different contractors to NOT finish it. VO In the 2017/2018 financial year, the municipality set aside R12.5 million for its construction… by 2020 the budget had doubled. UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA; COMMUNITY MEMBER SUBTITLES 03:48 - 03:50 Sir, this stadium is a disappointment though, if we are being honest. Yes, if we are being honest. VO But, 50 km away, in eNgcobo, things were about to get worse: Here, allleged corruption and incompetence had seen yet another promise broken. VO I’m met by community activist, Tando Tunce. UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE; SANCO SECRETARY 01:28 - 01:39 So, Tando, maybe you can tell us, where are we, what is this place and what is it supposed to be? This place is supposed to be a stadium, but when you look at it, it’s a bush that has things that show that there is somewhat of a stadium. VO This stadium was once at the heart of the district. UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE; SANCO SECRETARY 02:28 - 02:35 It was a beautiful place that encouraged us and all the young people from the villages had a dream that one day they would come play sports here. VO In 2015 the sportsground was approved for an upgrade… ..with stands and a proper athletics rubber track already in place… it only needed a little facelift… UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE; SANCO SECRETARY 03:25 - 03:37 This stadium was set to be built for R13,7 million but when it was built they topped up by an amount of R10 million to try ensure that the stadium is completed. 03:47 - 03:54 it was found that there was corruption happening in this stadium which led to halting the building process. VO Turns out, much like Centane and Sakhisizwe, it boasts features like toilets without plumbing or electricity… with predictable results. UPS CLAIRE I know as a CB presenter I’m supposed to go anywhere, but I think I’m going to stay outside for this one…. VO But 23.7 million did buy some stands and a netball court. UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE; SANCO SECRETARY 02:54 - 03:10 We feel extremely hurt as the people from eNgcobo from the players and organizers of soccer functions to the people at large because soccer and other sports help remove the youth from drugs. V/O In a statement - Dr AB Xuma Local Municipality confirmed that the project is still suspended due to substandard work and administration by the appointed contractor. VO We sought answers from the Eastern Cape Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs. VO After days of negotiation, the MEC agreed to an interview… VO But, after waiting for more than an hour, the MEC’s spokesperson and Chief of Staff appeared. Our cameras were rolling. UPS The interview is canceled for today VO But, not even the online interview materialised. LINK I have been stood up for the second time by COGTA MEC, Mr Zolile Williams.He had agreed to do a virtual interview with us to discuss these unfinished projects, but right now, not even his office is answering our calls. V/O The MEC later expressed disappointment with the state of the abandoned stadiums as these were meant to benefit local communities. But he says 60% of all sports facilities and stadiums built in the past seven-and-a-half years are in good condition, adding that some are state of the art facilities in rural towns like Cofimvaba and Ntabankulu. The MEC confirmed that investigations are underway in respect of the abandoned stadiums and that those responsible will be held accountable. LINK It's frustrating when money is allocated to build a facility and instead of just doing what you were meant to do with the money, there is nothing to show for it. And who suffers most? Children. Young people in the community, those with talent but have no opportunity to develop that talent. VO We leave amid Promises broken and unanswered questions. PROMO 1 21” Big money wasted and communities left with broken promises.. UPSOUND: TANDO TUNCE It was a beautiful place that encouraged us and all the young people from the villages had a dream that one day they would come play sports here. The Eastern Cape is scattered with substandard, incomplete projects intended to improve the lives of the residents… PROMO 2 21” So-called State-of-the-art facilities built for the people of the Eastern Cape… UPSOUND: LUNGISILE XEKETHWANA They run barefoot, they get cut under their feet leaving them with sores because this cement has open cracks and crumbling. Are communities benefiting from the millions being spent? PROMO 3 21” Incomplete, defunct sports stadiums and a taxi rank without working toilets… UPSOUND: XOLANI SOMANA People have no place to relieve themselves when they need the loo, they have to use the bush. LINK this is R6.8 million rand! The EC, a province of broken promises…

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A Trail of Broken Promises and Squandered Funds in the Eastern Cape...
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Uncovering the hidden realities behind the facade of development in the Eastern Cape and exposing the cost of incomplete projects and hold accountable those responsible for the mismanagement of public funds. The pursuit of accountability for years-old projects that have been abandoned, showcasing the ongoing lack of oversight and transparency in local government spending.
metadata.Summary: Amidst the buzz of provincial elections, Carte Blanche sets out to uncover a shadowy reality lurking beneath the surface of the Eastern Cape's development landscape. While the spotlight often shines on big-ticket projects and political promises, our investigation aims to shed light on the trail of incomplete projects left in the wake of mismanagement and controversy. This will be a news report. At the heart of our story are the communities of the Eastern Cape, whose hopes for improved infrastructure and amenities have been dashed by a series of failed projects. From the bustling streets of Centane to the tranquil fields of eNgcobo, we will journey through the province to witness firsthand the remnants of projects that never reached fruition.
metadata.Further information: Our investigation will start In Centane, our cameras will capture the surreal sight of a taxi rank that swallowed a whopping 6.4 million rand in public funds, yet fails to serve its intended purpose. Through investigative documents and interviews with stakeholders and officials, we will unravel the tangled web of bureaucracy and mismanagement that allowed such a debacle to occur. We will turn our attention to the eNgcobo sports field, where 10 million rand vanished into thin air, leaving behind nothing but a desolate landscape and the echoes of broken promises. With drone footage and eyewitness accounts, we will paint a vivid picture of the human cost of unfinished projects and the toll they take on communities striving for progress. Moving eastward, we will delve into the case of Sakhisizwe Local Municipality, where 23 million rand was poured into a sports facility that stands as a stark reminder of wasted resources and broken promises. With photographic evidence in hand, we will reveal the stark juxtaposition between the grand visions of the project and its current state of disrepair. Emalahleni Local Municipality, where a staggering 11 million rand was allocated to an incomplete project now reduced to nothing more than overgrown grass. Through on-the-ground interviews and expert analysis, we will uncover the reasons behind the project's abandonment and examine the repercussions for local residents left in its wake. Expose the truth behind the facade of development in the Eastern Cape, holding accountable those responsible for the squandering of public funds and the betrayal of public trust. In a province rife with political maneuvering and electoral fervor, our story will serve as a sobering reminder of the real-world consequences of incomplete projects and the urgent need for transparency and accountability in governance.
